dossier.purpose: Phoenix (PyPI arize-phoenix 20.19.0; src/phoenix/version.py:1) is a self-hostable AI observability and evaluation server. It receives OpenTelemetry/OpenInference traces (OTLP/HTTP protobuf POST /v1/traces on :6006, OTLP/gRPC on :4317). It stores them with annotations, datasets, experiments, prompts and cost data in SQLite (default) or PostgreSQL. It serves a web UI, REST (/v1) and GraphQL APIs, an in-process MCP server (/mcp), and a Playground plus background experiment runner that call external LLM providers. It also ships Python/TypeScript clients and a Node CLI (px). Facts mapped to the stated need questions, no judgement: (1) OTLP receiver: traces only; no receiver/processor/exporter pipeline and no server-side privacy filter (masking is client-side). (2) Store for OTLP usage metrics: none (no OTLP metrics endpoint or tables; the UI 'metrics' are time series computed from stored spans). (3) Store for OTLP events/logs: none. (4) Dashboards: the built-in web UI (per-project Metrics dashboard, span/trace/session tables) over Phoenix's own span database only; custom dashboards/alerting are pointed to the commercial Arize AX (docs/phoenix/tracing/llm-traces/metrics.mdx:31-33). (5) Traces + datasets + experiments store: yes (spans, versioned datasets with splits, experiments/runs/evaluations; Playground, Span Replay, server-side experiment runner, client run_experiment). (6) Local model server: none; Phoenix only calls model servers as a client (Ollama via OLLAMA_BASE_URL, OpenAI-compatible custom base URLs), and its own /v1/chat/completions proxy states 'Phoenix is not an AI gateway'. Claude Code/Codex: no handling of their native OTLP metrics/logs was found; the documented integrations are MCP/skills plugins in this repo and hook-based session-tracing plugins in a separate repo (Arize-ai/coding-harness-tracing) that emit OpenInference spans.

claims.claim: Tracing: 'Trace your LLM application's runtime using OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation.'
Datasets: 'Create versioned datasets of examples for experimentation, evaluation, and fine-tuning.'
Experiments: 'Track and evaluate changes to prompts, LLMs, and retrieval.'
Playground: 'Optimize prompts, compare models, adjust parameters, and replay traced LLM calls.'
Remote MCP Server: 'Connect Claude Code, Cursor, and other MCP clients directly to your Phoenix instance's /mcp endpoint to query traces, datasets, experiments, and more.'

'Phoenix is vendor and language agnostic with out-of-the-box support for popular frameworks (... Claude Agent SDK ...) and LLM providers (... LiteLLM, and more)'; auto-instrumentation comes from the separate OpenInference project.
'Phoenix runs practically anywhere, including your local machine, a containerized deployment, or in the cloud.'
'Phoenix is open-source and self-hosted.' (managed alternative: Arize AX)
'Install Phoenix via pip or conda': `pip install arize-phoenix` then `phoenix serve`, or `uvx arize-phoenix serve`.
`npx @arizeai/phoenix-cli setup` (or `px setup`): 'Setup detects your framework and LLM provider, installs the right OpenInference instrumentation, and wires up trace export.'
Phoenix container images are available via Docker Hub and deployable with Docker or the Helm chart.

Three surfaces let coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, others) work with traces, datasets and experiments: the CLI (`npx @arizeai/phoenix-cli`), Skills (.agents/skills/) and the Remote MCP Server (/mcp).

Telemetry: 'By default, Phoenix collects basic web analytics (e.g., page views, UI interactions)... None of your trace data, evaluation results, or any sensitive information is ever collected.' Opt out with PHOENIX_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false.
License: 'licensed under the terms of the Elastic License 2.0 (ELv2)'; portions are patent protected (IP_NOTICE).

install.command: pip install arize-phoenix   # then: phoenix serve
docker compose up --build   (docs compose file uses image arizephoenix/phoenix:latest + postgres; the repo's docker-compose.yml builds from ./Dockerfile)

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - Linux is the primary CI target: daily PyPI smoke test pip / uv pip / uv tool run installs on ubuntu-latest and polls /healthz (.github/workflows/pypi-smoke-test.yml:26-78); unit tests on ubuntu-latest in the scheduled all-platforms run (.github/workflows/python-all-platforms.yml:56-67) and on the oss-4-core-runner label per PR (.github/workflows/python-CI.yml:582-590); Docker images for linux/amd64 (.github/workflows/docker-build-release.yml:44); required C-extension arize-phoenix-sqlean ships manylinux wheels for cp311-cp314 (packages/phoenix-sqlean/cibuildwheel.toml:8,19-20).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - no mention of WSL/WSL2 in the README, docs, workflows or code (searched the checkout excluding lockfiles/notebooks). Linux install paths (pip, Docker) and Windows CI exist (python-all-platforms.yml:67), but WSL2 itself is neither documented nor tested.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes - unit tests run on macos-latest (py3.11 and 3.14, sqlite) in the weekday-scheduled all-platforms workflow (.github/workflows/python-all-platforms.yml:5-8,56-67; the runner architecture is not stated in the file); the required arize-phoenix-sqlean extension builds macOS arm64 and x86_64 wheels (packages/phoenix-sqlean/cibuildwheel.toml:22-23); the Dockerfile mentions Apple-Silicon arm64 images (Dockerfile:22-24) and release images are multi-arch linux/amd64+linux/arm64 (docker-build-release.yml:44). The README has no explicit supported-platform table.
platforms.gpu: no - Phoenix does not use a GPU: no CUDA/torch/GPU dependency in pyproject.toml:23-81 and no GPU/CUDA references in src/ (only 'nvidia/' dataset URLs in fixture descriptions, src/phoenix/trace/fixtures.py:265-286); model inference is delegated to external providers.

integrations.cli: yes - Python console scripts `phoenix` and `arize-phoenix` (subcommands serve, trace-fixture, db migrate, datagen) (pyproject.toml:84-86; src/phoenix/server/main.py:17-30; src/phoenix/server/cli/commands/serve.py:160-211). integrations.sdk_or_api: yes - ingest: OTLP/HTTP POST /v1/traces (protobuf only) and OTLP/gRPC :4317 (traces only) (src/phoenix/server/api/routers/v1/traces.py:440-509; src/phoenix/server/grpc_server.py:33-52,110). integrations.claude_code_or_codex: yes (read-side and via a separate tracing repo), with limits. (a) This repo is a Claude Code plugin marketplace (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json; plugins/claude/arize-phoenix/.mcp.json registers the Phoenix MCP server at ${endpoint}/mcp) and a Codex plugin marketplace (.agents/plugins/marketplace.json; plugins/codex/arize-phoenix/.mcp.json plus scripts/phoenix-mcp, which bridges via `npx --yes mcp-remote`) (docs/phoenix/integrations/developer-tools/coding-agents.mdx:51-221). (b) Agent skills in .agents/skills/phoenix-cli, phoenix-evals, phoenix-tracing (README.md:269-279). (c) `px setup` can hand app instrumentation to a detected claude/codex/opencode/cursor binary (js/packages/phoenix-cli/src/setup/agents/registry.ts:1-16). (d) Session tracing of Claude Code, the Codex CLI and the Claude Agent SDK is done by hook-based plugins from a separate repository, Arize-ai/coding-harness-tracing, which emit OpenInference spans to Phoenix and expose ARIZE_LOG_PROMPTS / ARIZE_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS / ARIZE_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT redaction flags (docs/phoenix/integrations/coding-agents/claude-code.mdx:9,84-102; docs/phoenix/integrations/coding-agents/codex.mdx:9,60-74); that code is not in this checkout and was not verified. (e) ATIF trajectory import for Claude Code/Codex runs exported through Harbor (docs/phoenix/tracing/how-to-tracing/importing-and-exporting-traces/importing-atif-trajectories.mdx:6-26). Not found: any code or doc consuming Claude Code or Codex native OTLP metrics/logs/events; CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY, OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER and OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER do not occur anywhere in the checkout (excluding lockfiles).

readme.telemetry_and_network: Analytics/phone-home: by default the web UI embeds a Scarf.sh tracking pixel, an the browser loads from https://static.scarf.sh/a.png?x-pxid= with referrerpolicy='no-referrer-when-downgrade' (src/phoenix/server/templates/index.html:155-157); the pixel id defaults to a hard-coded value (src/phoenix/config.py:3713-3723). FullStory loads only if PHOENIX_FULLSTORY_ORG is set (config.py:3700-3710; index.html:102-125). Master opt-out PHOENIX_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false (config.py:151-156,3683-3697; README.md:289; docs/phoenix/self-hosting/security/privacy.mdx:20-41). Docs state self-hosted trace/eval/dataset data is never sent to Arize or third parties (privacy.mdx:8). Other default outbound requests while PHOENIX_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_RESOURCES is true (default; config.py:157-162,3848-3853): Google Fonts (index.html:92-96); browser-side GitHub star-count and PyPI latest-version lookups (js/app/src/components/nav/GitHubStarCount.tsx:10; js/app/src/hooks/useLatestPhoenixVersion.ts:3,45); a server-side download of a CPython WASM sandbox binary from GitHub at startup when the WASM sandbox provider is allowed (all providers are allowed by default) (src/phoenix/server/sandbox/_download.py:25-33,148-171,193-198; config.py:865-878,1300-1315); PXI assistant tools: Mintlify-hosted docs MCP (src/phoenix/server/app.py:1102-1106; agents/capabilities/docs_mcp.py:14), web access and GitHub MCP at https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ (config.py:1436-1456). PHOENIX_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_RESOURCES=false disables all of these plus telemetry (privacy.mdx:43-53; network-security.mdx:157-185). The `--no-internet` CLI flag is declared but never read (src/phoenix/server/cli/commands/serve.py:152). Opt-in outbound: the server can export its own traces to an OTLP collector (src/phoenix/server/telemetry.py:38-68) and PXI assistant traces to a remote collector via PHOENIX_AGENTS_COLLECTOR_ENDPOINT (config.py:70-79); the Prometheus endpoint on :9090 is off by default (config.py:323-326; src/phoenix/server/prometheus.py:184). Required services/accounts: none for self-hosting; the default store is a SQLite file under ~/.phoenix (config.py:1150-1154,3374-3381), with optional PostgreSQL >=14 (docs/phoenix/self-hosting/architecture.mdx:13-32); no account is needed (README.md:64-67; terminal.mdx:12-18). LLM calls (Playground, evals, PXI) go only to operator-configured providers, and the app does not validate custom base URLs (docs/phoenix/self-hosting/security/network-security.mdx:8-12,572-574). Listening: HTTP 0.0.0.0:6006 (UI, REST, GraphQL, MCP and OTLP/HTTP share the port) and gRPC [::]:4317, optional TLS/mTLS (config.py:3112-3121; grpc_server.py:95-109; serve.py:281-289,414-422); authentication is off by default (config.py:1237-1241).

code.architecture: Single Python ASGI service (FastAPI/Starlette + uvicorn) with a bundled React 19/Relay UI built from js/app into src/phoenix/server/static. src/phoenix/server/main.py -> cli/commands/serve.py -> app.py:create_app mounts the REST /v1 routers (src/phoenix/server/api/routers/v1/*.py), GraphQL (strawberry; src/phoenix/server/api/), the MCP app at /mcp (src/phoenix/server/mcp_server.py, mcp/skills), agent/PXI routers (src/phoenix/server/agents/) and the static UI (app.py:1147-1153,1233-1236,1287). Ingestion: the OTLP/HTTP handler (routers/v1/traces.py) and an asyncio gRPC server (grpc_server.py) decode OTLP spans (src/phoenix/trace/otel.py; OTel GenAI -> OpenInference conversion in src/phoenix/trace/gen_ai/conversion.py) and enqueue them on a bounded queue drained by a bulk inserter (src/phoenix/db/bulk_inserter.py; HTTP 503 when the queue is full, traces.py:431-437; HTTP 507 when DB storage thresholds are exceeded, src/phoenix/server/authorization.py:130-149). Project routing uses the x-project-name header or the openinference.project.name resource attribute (traces.py:706-728). Storage: SQLAlchemy models (src/phoenix/db/models.py: projects, traces, spans, span/trace/session annotations, datasets/versions/examples/splits, experiments/runs/jobs, prompts, evaluators, span_costs, users/API keys, sandbox configs, agent sessions), Alembic migrations (src/phoenix/db/migrations), SQLite through the bundled sqlean fork (src/phoenix/db/engines.py:14,28; packages/phoenix-sqlean) or PostgreSQL via asyncpg (extra [pg]). Background daemons (src/phoenix/server/daemons/): experiment runner/sweeper, span cost calculator, DB disk-usage monitor, system settings. Code-evaluator sandboxes: WASM, Deno, Monty, E2B, Daytona, Vercel, Modal (src/phoenix/server/sandbox/). Provider clients for Playground/evals (src/phoenix/server/api/helpers/playground_clients.py) and the PXI assistant on pydantic-ai (src/phoenix/server/agents/). Sibling packages: packages/phoenix-client, phoenix-evals, phoenix-otel, phoenix-sqlean; js/packages/phoenix-{cli,client,evals,otel,mcp,config,testing}; helm/ chart.
code.packaging_and_release: release-please on push to main manages versions and tags such as arize-phoenix-v20.19.0 via .release-please-manifest.json and then dispatches publish.yaml (.github/workflows/release.yml:1-24). publish.yaml builds the UI with pnpm, runs `uv build` (hatchling) to make a wheel and sdist, checks the wheel for bundled UI assets and with check-wheel-contents, and publishes to PyPI through PyPI Trusted Publishing/OIDC (environment `pypi`, id-token: write, pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish) (.github/workflows/publish.yaml:83-164). The same flow covers arize-phoenix-client/-evals/-otel (publish.yaml:166-275) and arize-phoenix-sqlean, built with cibuildwheel for manylinux, macOS x86_64/arm64 and Windows AMD64/ARM64 on cp311-cp314 plus an sdist (publish.yaml:284-357; packages/phoenix-sqlean/cibuildwheel.toml:8-26). Tag-triggered docker-build-release.yml builds Docker Hub images arizephoenix/phoenix for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 in root (unsuffixed tags such as latest), nonroot and debug variants on distroless python3-debian13, pushed by digest and merged into manifest lists; builds use BuildKit `--provenance mode=max --sbom true` (docker-build-release.yml:7,44-128; .github/actions/docker-build-image/action.yml:117-133). The Dockerfile pins the CPython WASM binary by SHA-256 (Dockerfile:101-117). The Helm chart is packaged and pushed to oci://registry-1.docker.io/arizephoenix (.github/workflows/helm-release.yaml:45-49), and a post-release job opens a PR bumping kustomize/Helm versions (docker-build-release.yml:130-168). npm packages are published via changesets with NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE=true (.github/workflows/typescript-packages-publish.yml:48-65). No checksum files, cosign/sigstore signatures or explicit PyPI attestation inputs appear under .github (searched for cosign|sigstore|attest|slsa|checksum|gpg; only the docker provenance/sbom flags and npm provenance match). Dev preview builds can be published from a feature branch (publish.yaml:469-646). uv is pinned (`required-version = "==0.12.19"`) with `exclude-newer = "3 days"` (pyproject.toml:462-463), and Actions are pinned by commit SHA.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:49 'Tracing - Trace your LLM application's runtime using OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation.'

risks: No OTLP metrics/logs path. The gRPC server registers only the trace service (src/phoenix/server/grpc_server.py:5-12,110) and the only OTLP HTTP route is POST /v1/traces, protobuf-only (HTTP 415 for any other content type; src/phoenix/server/api/routers/v1/traces.py:440-486). MetricsService, LogsService, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs, ExportMetrics and ExportLogs occur nowhere in the checkout, and there are no metric/log-record tables (src/phoenix/db/models.py). docs/phoenix/production-guide.mdx:19,37,45 nonetheless speak of spans, metrics and logs reaching Phoenix. No handling of Claude Code/Codex native telemetry settings (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY, OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER, OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER) exists in README, docs or src.

No server-side privacy filter for ingested telemetry. Spans are decoded and stored as received (src/phoenix/trace/otel.py:97-134). Masking is client-side via OpenInference TraceConfig / OPENINFERENCE_HIDE_* variables (docs/phoenix/tracing/how-to-tracing/advanced/masking-span-attributes.mdx:8-45) or the separate coding-harness-tracing plugins' ARIZE_LOG_* flags (docs/phoenix/integrations/coding-agents/claude-code.mdx:84-102), whose code is outside this checkout and unverified. src/phoenix/server/redaction.py only encrypts transient secrets (redaction.py:1-21).

Open-by-default exposure. HTTP binds 0.0.0.0:6006 and gRPC [::]:4317 (src/phoenix/config.py:3112-3118; src/phoenix/server/grpc_server.py:109); authentication is off unless PHOENIX_ENABLE_AUTH is set (config.py:1237-1241); the /mcp app is mounted by default and is not wrapped in BearerAuthGuard when auth is off, with MCP code-mode `execute` default-on (config.py:3656-3661; src/phoenix/server/app.py:1018,1233-1236); the repo docker-compose.yml uses postgres/postgres credentials and publishes 6006 and 4317 (docker-compose.yml:8-19).

Default outbound requests unless PHOENIX_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_RESOURCES=false: Scarf pixel, Google Fonts, GitHub star-count and PyPI version lookups from the browser; a startup download of a WASM sandbox binary from GitHub; PXI docs/web/GitHub tools (src/phoenix/config.py:157-162,3695-3723; src/phoenix/server/templates/index.html:92-96,155-157; src/phoenix/server/sandbox/_download.py:25-33,193-198; src/phoenix/server/app.py:1102-1106). The `--no-internet` flag is declared but never read (src/phoenix/server/cli/commands/serve.py:152).

Not a model server or gateway. There is no inference-serving code and no GPU/CUDA use (pyproject.toml:23-81). Local models are reachable only as client targets: OLLAMA_BASE_URL or a custom OpenAI-compatible base_url (src/phoenix/server/api/helpers/playground_clients.py:3672-3701; src/phoenix/db/types/model_provider.py:211-220). The built-in /v1/chat/completions proxy says 'Phoenix is not an AI gateway', warns that routing production calls competes with trace ingestion, and does not support tool calling (src/phoenix/server/api/routers/v1/chat_completions.py:400-404). The app does not validate provider base URLs, so SSRF controls must be at the network layer (docs/phoenix/self-hosting/security/network-security.mdx:16-24,572-574).

Licensing is mixed. The server, arize-phoenix-evals and the JS workspace root are Elastic License 2.0 (LICENSE:1-45; pyproject.toml:6; packages/phoenix-evals/pyproject.toml:6; js/package.json:16), a source-available license that forbids offering the software as a hosted/managed service and circumventing license-key functionality (LICENSE:10-12). IP_NOTICE:3 lists patents US 11,315,043 and 11,615,345, and the README still calls the project 'open-source' (README.md:66-67). arize-phoenix-client, -otel and most @arizeai JS packages are Apache-2.0 (packages/phoenix-client/pyproject.toml:6; packages/phoenix-otel/pyproject.toml:6; js/packages/phoenix-cli/package.json:15). Contributions require a CLA (.github/workflows/cla.yml:24-31).

Footprint and platform limits. 54 direct Python runtime dependencies including pandas, scipy, scikit-learn, pyarrow, pydantic-ai and fastmcp (pyproject.toml:23-81) plus a required C extension, arize-phoenix-sqlean, whose wheels cover manylinux/macOS/Windows on cp311-cp314 only; musllinux and PyPy fall back to an sdist build needing a C toolchain (packages/phoenix-sqlean/cibuildwheel.toml:5-8); Python >=3.11,<3.15 (pyproject.toml:5). SQLite is the single-node default and PostgreSQL >=14 is recommended for production (docs/phoenix/self-hosting/architecture.mdx:13-32). The only published measurements are first-party LLM-judge accuracy tables; no ingestion throughput/latency or local-model figures were found in the docs.

Maintenance and policy signals. SECURITY.md lists only 2.x.x as supported while the release is 20.19.0 (SECURITY.md:5-9; src/phoenix/version.py:1). MIGRATION.md records breaking changes for every major from v13 to v20 (MIGRATION.md:3,32,142,156,168,208,212,434). .github/dependabot.yml is an unfilled template (package-ecosystem is empty, line 8) while dependency upgrades run through an LLM-driven weekly workflow (.github/workflows/claude-weekly-deps-upgrade.yml:1-6). Full macOS/Windows test legs run only on a weekday schedule, not per PR (python-all-platforms.yml:5-8), and the macOS e2e leg is disabled (.github/workflows/playwright.yaml:102).
